clue.text: End of constipation — one mostly passed liquid thanks to these

definitions.text: End of constipation — one mostly passed liquid thanks to these

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so these letters are poured into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of constipation is used

parts.note: its last letter is N

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so one loses its final letter

parts.note: one without its last letter gives ON

explanation.surface: A frank remark about laxatives: thanks to these, a constipated patient finally found relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' gives N, the last letter of 'constipation'; 'one' with 'mostly' cut short is ON; 'passed' is taken as written. 'Liquid' stirs NONPASSED into the answer, and the whole clue describes what the pods do.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna pods are a traditional herbal laxative, taken precisely to bring constipation to an end.

clue.text: Reminder one with virus is in a bad way

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in a sorry state, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A warning that someone who has caught a virus is feeling poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' and 'virus' together are rearranged, signalled by 'is in a bad way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a keepsake kept to bring back memories of a place or event.

clue.text: Essence of cake that's rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A baker considering the key quality of a cake as it rises in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Rising cakes sound like baking, but in a down light 'rising' turns BUN upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nub of something is its core or central point, the crux of the matter.

clue.text: If absolutely necessary, un robinet, ein Hahn, un rubinetto, or üna spina

parts.words: un robinet, ein Hahn, un rubinetto
parts.note: each phrase means a tap, in French, German and Italian
üna spina is a tap in Romansh, the fourth national language, completing the set spoken in Switzerland, whose international code is CH

explanation.surface: A phrasebook list giving the word for a tap in several European languages, for use in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrases all mean 'a tap', and adding Romansh makes the four languages exactly those of Switzerland, CH on car stickers and web addresses: so the clue reads 'a tap in CH'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom at a pinch means if really needed, in a tight spot, as a last resort.

clue.text: Warning of short period without cover

indicators.note: the cover is the top of a down entry, so the first letter is removed
short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a moment is a brief period of time

explanation.surface: An alert about spending a brief time exposed with no shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the last letter of MOMENT to give MOMEN, and 'without cover' then removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent foretelling something, often trouble, ahead.

clue.text: Can it sell out and cease trading?

parts.note: can it is slang for be quiet, shut up
to shop someone is to inform on or betray them

explanation.surface: A worried question whether a business can sell all its stock and close down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sell out' reads like clearing stock, but here it means betray, which is SHOP in British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut up shop is an idiom for closing a business or stopping work for good.

clue.text: Responsible person conserves energy in race

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it held within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a carer is the person responsible for looking after someone
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sensible athlete pacing themselves to save energy during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a noun, a contest, but it is the verb: to career is to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to move swiftly and uncontrollably, hurtling along as in a dash.

clue.text: A good and upstanding prophet concurs

indicators.note: in a down light, standing up means written bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a seer is one who foresees, a prophet

explanation.surface: A worthy and honest prophet gives assent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' reads as a compliment to the prophet, but it turns SEER upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to concur, to be of the same opinion as someone else.

clue.text: Investigation moving quickly to snare Stone at last

indicators.note: a snare traps something inside it, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: haring means running fast, like a hare

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of Stone

parts.note: its last letter is E

explanation.surface: Detectives racing to catch a man called Stone at long last.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing is a formal examination of a case, such as a court or tribunal inquiry.

clue.text: Finish on a high, picking up answer, sort of

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to end a performance on a triumphant note after collecting the right answer, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a high' looks like a happy finish, but 'high' is the anagram signal: FINISHONA plus A (answer) is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fashion means after a manner, to some extent, not entirely properly: roughly.

clue.text: Speechless with anger when duke denied offence

indicators.note: denied means refused, so this letter is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: A nobleman, refused something, is left speechless and furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Denied' removes D (duke) from DUMB RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking umbrage means taking offence; umbrage is a feeling of resentment or being slighted.

clue.text: Ate modern cooking in place of worship

indicators.note: cooking means mixing up and transforming ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dined on contemporary cuisine inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the great Gothic cathedral in Paris, a famous church.

clue.text: Sign backing top mathematician

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act
a lid is the top of a container

explanation.surface: A star sign supporting the finest maths expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like support, but it reverses CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek geometer whose Elements founded classical geometry.

clue.text: Lucky escape, as Conservative is defeated with experience

parts.note: to lose is to be defeated
to have something, such as a good time, is to experience it

explanation.surface: A Conservative candidate narrowly avoiding disaster at an election despite seasoned campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is an idiom for a narrow escape from danger or disaster.

clue.text: Give running account of one leaving red books at Eton's entrance

indicators.note: leaving means going out of, so this letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a red, or commie, is an informal word for a communist
I is the Roman numeral for one
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: its first letter is E

explanation.surface: Describing a lone communist walking out of a public school with his books.
explanation.walkthrough: COMMIE with I ('one') 'leaving' is COMME, then NT, AT and the 'entrance' of Eton, E. Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: To commentate is to provide a live spoken description of an event, as a sports broadcaster does.

clue.text: Photographers capturing her bum, possibly

indicators.note: capturing means taking hold of, so the photographers enclose the other letters

parts.note: paps is short for paparazzi, press photographers

indicators.note: bum in British slang means poor or bad, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Paparazzi snapping a celebrity's backside, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like the photographers' target, but it is a slangy anagram signal turning HER into ERH.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps is an adverb expressing uncertainty, meaning maybe.

clue.text: Press X to get medal

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: A video game instruction: hit the X button to earn a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military decoration for bravery.

clue.text: Make labs seem chaotic

indicators.note: chaotic means in total disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone renders the laboratories a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to construct or put together, as with a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Sperm densities regularly start to rise in academic session

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every other one starting with the first
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is R

explanation.surface: A lab report noting that sperm counts keep climbing during term time.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is one of the two halves of a university year, a term of teaching.

clue.text: Liquor that Guy drinks at home following low points

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed after the earlier ones

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
N and S are compass points, north and south

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: he stands for a man, a guy
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man drinking spirits at home after some low moments in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low points' looks like bad times, but 'low' is MOO and 'points' are compass points NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled spirit, bootleg whisky made out of sight of the law.

clue.text: River that can be seen to be losing volume, which is ludicrous

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so this letter is removed

parts.note: visible means able to be seen

explanation.surface: A river that is visibly shrinking in size, which seems absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, so silly it provokes ridicule.

clue.text: It partly inspired rages

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something was to blame for provoking furious outbursts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the definition: a red rag is a thing that provokes anger, as one to a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A red rag, as to a bull, is anything that provokes fury, which is exactly what this clue says it did.

clue.text: One offering shot of weapon to stop outlaw

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so this piece fills the middle of the other

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A gunman firing to stop a bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a gun, but it is a shot of spirits poured over the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman serves drinks, including shots of spirits, from behind a pub counter.

clue.text: Chap that is squirreling away Euros, primarily?

definitions.text: Chap that is squirreling away Euros, primarily?

indicators.note: squirreling away means hiding something inside, as a squirrel stores nuts

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: its first letter is E

explanation.surface: A man hoarding his euro coins instead of spending them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone stashing money away rather than spending it is a stingy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is an informal word for a stingy or unkind person, a miser.

clue.text: Macron, perhaps, rejected help to get attacker

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: aid means help
a critic attacks something verbally

explanation.surface: French president Emmanuel Macron turned down assistance to deal with an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Macron' looks like the French president, but a macron is the bar over a long vowel, as in ā.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is a mark added to a letter to show pronunciation, and the macron is one example.

clue.text: King briefly drinks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short form of the name Charles, as with King Charles
second meaning: the plural of cha, a slang word for tea

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain cha (or char) is informal for a cup of tea, so chas are teas.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a contracted form of Charles and the plural of a slang term for tea.

clue.text: Home of slightly boring headwear

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hat is headwear
a bit means slightly

explanation.surface: The residence of a rather dull hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling into the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where an animal or plant lives.

clue.text: Bit romantic partner on the way up after scratching bottom

indicators.note: in a down light, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters are reversed
scratching means striking off, and the bottom of the word is its last letter, removed before the turn

parts.note: a date is someone you go out with romantically

explanation.surface: A girlfriend climbing the stairs while scratching her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the last letter of DATE ('scratching bottom') to get DAT, then send it 'on the way up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a small amount, a little.

clue.text: I don't laugh a long time after everyone else

definitions.note: the definition is the self-description of a person who never laughs, a noun

parts.note: an age is a very long time
last means coming after all the others

explanation.surface: Someone who only gets the joke long after everyone else has laughed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: an agelast would say 'I don't laugh'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agelast is a rare word for a humourless person who never laughs, from Greek.

clue.text: Model sneered at Cockney

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion model was looked down on by a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End, so an East Ender.
explanation.definitionFit: An East Ender is a person from the East End of London, the traditional home of Cockneys.
